intent: Test turn authority alone against the iteration 1 design by reducing mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg, keeping the ±0.045 m sensor span that reduced oval line losses and the 0.10 m wheel track. The aim is to cut yaw inertia so the robot turns back before reaching the 0.06 m off-track limit on the s-bend and slalom, where line losses stayed at 1.0.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that widening the sensors cut oval line losses (1.05 to 0.55) but did not reduce max_error on s-bend or slalom, and the combined change scored lower (55.8 vs 62.3) because oval progress fell. Iteration 1 also changed wheel_track, so its effect is confounded. Next, check whether mass 0.6 kg brings s-bend and slalom line losses to 0 and max_error below 0.055 m. Also check whether oval progress recovers. If it does, the mass lever is confirmed. If not, test wheel_track 0.09 m next, and treat the oval progress shortfall as a speed (controller) issue.
rationale: Iteration 1 scored 55.8 against 62.3 for the baseline, so the change did not help overall. The mixed results point to a specific fix. On the oval, line-loss events fell from 1.05 to 0.55 after the sensors were widened to ±0.045 m, so sensing reach helped there. But oval progress fell from 0.175 to 0.121, which cost more score than the loss reduction gained. On the s-bend and slalom, line-loss events stayed at 1.0 and max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.068, which is the Integrator's stated condition for turn authority being the constraint. Steering oscillation rose on those tracks (0.16 to 0.16 against 0.15), so the robot is reacting more, not less, and the extra reaction has not translated into recovery before the 0.06 m limit. The narrower wheel track (0.10 m) was tested together with the wider sensors, so its separate effect cannot be read. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m across the allowed body widths. Next, I follow the Integrator's pre-agreed rule for the constraint case: reduce mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. Yaw inertia falls from about 0.00312 to 0.00234 kg·m², so the robot should turn back faster for the same wheel differential. I keep the ±0.045 m sensor span, because the oval loss reduction is evidence it works, and I keep wheel_track at 0.10 m, so this iteration changes only mass against the iteration 1 design. This keeps the test clean. Expected result: line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall toward 0, max_error drops below about 0.055 m, and oval progress recovers as the robot can hold the line at higher speed. If line losses persist at 1 with max_error still at the limit, the next lever is wheel_track 0.09 m. If the robot now finishes but progress is low, the Integrator should raise base_speed rather than I change geometry further.
